patterns.name: Linear Arrangements with Grouped Block and Fixed Category Ends
patterns.description: Arranging a collection of items in a line where specific items must stay together as a single block and the ends of the line are restricted to members of a particular category.

patterns.name: Permutations Grouped Block with Internal Separation
patterns.description: Arrangements combining block grouping with internal separation conditions.

patterns.name: Permutations of Grouped Blocks Across Multiple Rows
patterns.description: Arranging multiple distinct groups of adjacent people across specified rows and seat configurations.

patterns.name: Permutations of Repeated Identical Items with Grouping
patterns.description: Arranging a collection of items containing identical elements when a particular group of identical items must be kept together.

patterns.name: Permutations of Repeated Items with Fixed Ends or Subtraction
patterns.description: Arranging items with repeated identical elements subject to specific end positions or separation constraints.

patterns.name: Permutations with Minimum Separation Distance Between Repeated Letters
patterns.description: Arranging letters of a word with repeated items where two identical letters must have at least a specified number of intervening letters.

patterns.name: Permutations Multiple Blocks
patterns.description: Arrangements where several distinct subsets must each stay together.

patterns.name: Permutations with Multiple Grouped Blocks
patterns.description: Arranging items of multiple distinct categories in a line such that all members of each category stay together, calculated as the product of the block permutations and the internal permutations within each block.

patterns.name: Permutations Nested Block with Separation
patterns.description: Complex permutations combining block constraints with separation of other items.

patterns.name: Permutations Where Specified Identical Items Are Not All Together
patterns.description: Finding the number of arrangements of a set of items with repetitions where a particular group of identical letters or items are not all together by subtracting the number of arrangements where they are grouped together from the total unrestricted arrangements.

patterns.name: Ordered Selection Permutations
patterns.description: Counting the number of ways to select and arrange r items from n distinct items using nPr.

patterns.name: Permutations of Multiset with Repeated Identical Elements
patterns.description: Arranging all items in a set containing multiple groups of identical elements by dividing the total factorial by the factorials of each group of identical elements.

patterns.name: Permutations with Repeated Letters
patterns.description: Arrangements of letters from words with duplicate characters.

patterns.name: Permutations with Separated Items Using the Gap Method
patterns.description: Arranging a set of objects such that certain items cannot be adjacent by placing the unconstrained items first and inserting the restricted items into the resulting spaces.

patterns.name: Permutations with Adjacent Block and Separated Pair Constraint
patterns.description: Arranging a set of items where one designated pair must remain adjacent while another designated pair must remain separated, evaluated by subtracting the double-adjacent case.

patterns.name: Permutations Subtraction Method
patterns.description: Finding arrangements satisfying a constraint by subtracting the complement from total arrangements.

patterns.name: Arrangements with Category Quotas and Case Partitioning
patterns.description: Forming codes or passwords of fixed length with at least one item from each category by partitioning selections into cases and arranging distinct elements.

patterns.name: Permutations with Fixed End Elements
patterns.description: Arranging a collection of items with specified items fixed at the first and last positions and permuting intermediate items with repetitions.

patterns.name: Permutations with Fixed Separation Between Repeated Letters
patterns.description: Arranging letters of a word with identical letters separated by a fixed number of intervening positions, counting valid slot pairs and permuting remaining letters.

patterns.name: Two-Stage Discrete Possibility Space
patterns.description: Using a possibility-space grid or ordered listing to evaluate probabilities of compound events from two discrete trials.

patterns.name: Probability from Combinations with Category Quotas
patterns.description: Evaluating classical probability by summing combination counts across acceptable category quotas divided by total combinations.

patterns.name: Probability from Combinations Ratio
patterns.description: Finding probabilities by dividing combinations of favorable outcomes by total combinations.

patterns.name: Probability from Permutations
patterns.description: Calculating probability as favorable arrangements divided by total arrangements.

patterns.name: Probability of Objects Not All Adjacent via Complement
patterns.description: Finding the probability that a group of distinct objects are not all adjacent by subtracting the together-block count from total permutations.

patterns.name: Probability That Two Specific Individuals Are Assigned to the Same Subgroup
patterns.description: Finding the probability that two named individuals are placed into the same subgroup when a population is randomly partitioned into groups of unequal sizes.

patterns.name: Proportional Subdivision of Normal Classification Category
patterns.description: Using a conditional fraction or ratio to determine the unconditional probability of a subdivision within an upper or lower normal region.

patterns.name: Qualitative Comparison of Normal Probabilities Under Parameter Changes
patterns.description: Explaining the effect of changing variance or standard deviation on the spread and central tail probabilities of a normal model without numerical calculation.

patterns.name: Quartiles from Discrete Data
patterns.description: Determining lower quartile, median, and upper quartile from ordered lists or stem-and-leaf diagrams.

patterns.name: Finding Medians and Quartiles from Stem-and-Leaf Diagram
patterns.description: Locating the median and lower/upper quartiles from ordered leaves in a stem-and-leaf diagram and computing the interquartile range.

patterns.name: Estimating Frequencies Exceeding a Threshold from Graph
patterns.description: Reading cumulative frequency at a given threshold on the horizontal axis and subtracting from the total frequency.

patterns.name: Probability All Successive Independent Draws Yield Distinct Categories
patterns.description: Finding the probability that in k draws with replacement from k equally likely categories, every draw results in a different category, evaluated via k! / k^k.

patterns.name: Sampling Without Replacement Until First Success
patterns.description: Calculating the exact probability of obtaining the first item of a target type on trial k in non-replacement sampling.

patterns.name: Seating Arrangements on a Specific Side of a Table
patterns.description: Arranging individuals across multiple tables where two specific people must sit together on the same side of a specified table.

patterns.name: Selection Without Replacement with at Least One Item from Each of Two Categories
patterns.description: Finding the probability of selecting items without replacement such that at least one item from each of two distinct categories is chosen, evaluated either by partitioning into mutually exclusive composition cases or by subtracting the complement of excluded category profiles.

patterns.name: Selecting Across Categories Using Complement of Single-Category Choices
patterns.description: Finding selections of items from multiple categories containing at least two different categories by subtracting single-category combinations from total combinations.

patterns.name: Selecting Items with Repetitions Subject to Unequal Frequency Conditions
patterns.description: Finding the number of selections of a specified size from a set containing repeated items where the counts of two particular items must be unequal, by systematically evaluating disjoint cases.

patterns.name: Probability of Selection with Repeated Items Using Combinations
patterns.description: Finding the probability that a random sample of items chosen without replacement contains specified frequencies of repeated categories by dividing favorable combination counts by total possible combinations.

patterns.name: Probability All Selected Items Have Distinct Categories Without Replacement
patterns.description: Calculating the probability that when multiple items are chosen without replacement from several categories, exactly one item is drawn from each distinct category.

patterns.name: Probability of at Least One Category Item in Selections Without Replacement
patterns.description: Evaluating the probability that at least one item of a specified type is selected in multiple successive draws without replacement by subtracting the probability of zero selections from 1.

patterns.name: Selection Without Replacement Probability via Combinations
patterns.description: Finding the probability of selecting a specified composition of items without replacement using combinations or hypergeometric products.

patterns.name: Selections with Frequency Comparison Restriction via Complement
patterns.description: Selecting an unranked sample from a multiset subject to a relative frequency condition between two letter types, evaluated by subtracting the violating complementary cases.

patterns.name: Selections with Simultaneous Lower and Upper Bounds on Categories
patterns.description: Selecting an unranked subset of letters from a multiset containing repeated items where specific categories are subject to simultaneous minimum and maximum frequency constraints.

patterns.name: Selections from Sets Containing Repeated Elements
patterns.description: Forming unordered selections of items from a set containing repeated items by partitioning into mutually exclusive cases based on the frequency of the repeated item.

patterns.name: Sequential Draws Without Replacement in a Turn-Based Game
patterns.description: Evaluating path probabilities and conditional probabilities in a turn-based game where two players draw without replacement until one achieves a target count of items.

patterns.name: Sequential Multi-Attempt Game Completion and Conditional Probability
patterns.description: Evaluating overall success in a multi-level sequential game where each level allows multiple attempts with independent probabilities, and computing conditional probabilities of specific failure counts given overall completion.

patterns.name: Sequential Multi-Trial Transition Probabilities and Event Sequences
patterns.description: Evaluating probabilities of specific success/failure sequences where each trial outcome conditionally determines the success probability of the subsequent trial.

patterns.name: Sequential Selection of Multiple Structured Subgroups from Categorized Pools
patterns.description: Problems requiring the selection of multiple distinct groups or teams where each team requires fixed quotas from several categories without replacement.

patterns.name: Simultaneous Equations for Normal Mean and Standard Deviation
patterns.description: Forming two linear equations in mean and standard deviation from upper and lower normal tail probabilities and solving simultaneously.

patterns.name: Solving Unknown Component Probabilities from Compound Score Events
patterns.description: Setting up and solving polynomial equations for individual outcome probabilities from compound scores of independent spinners or dice.

patterns.name: Standard Deviation from Summary Statistics
patterns.description: Calculating standard deviation from sum of x and sum of x^2.

patterns.name: Calculating Cumulative Normal Probability
patterns.description: Problems standardising a continuous random variable X ~ N(mu, sigma^2) and finding cumulative probability P(X < x) using standard normal tables.

patterns.name: Normal Standardization with Proportional Mean and Standard Deviation
patterns.description: Evaluating standard normal probabilities when the mean is specified as a constant multiple of the standard deviation (e.g. mu = k sigma).

patterns.name: Stem-and-Leaf Median and IQR
patterns.description: Finding median and interquartile range directly from an ordered stem-and-leaf diagram.

patterns.name: Probability of Sum of Independent Discrete Spinners Below Threshold
patterns.description: Calculating the probability that the sum of scores from three independent spinners is less than or equal to a given threshold by listing and evaluating all mutually exclusive outcome combinations.

patterns.name: Expected Frequency from Symmetric Normal Central Interval
patterns.description: Exploiting symmetry around the mean to evaluate a central normal interval probability and scaling by total trials to estimate an expected integer frequency.

patterns.name: Testing Event Independence
patterns.description: Verifying whether two events are statistically independent by checking whether P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B).

patterns.name: Testing Independence Product Rule
patterns.description: Testing if P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B) to verify independence of events.

patterns.name: Sum of Three Dice Threshold in Geometric Distribution
patterns.description: Evaluating the probability of an extreme sum on three dice and using it as the single-trial success parameter in geometric waiting time problems.

patterns.name: Total Probability in Two-Stage Transfer Experiment
patterns.description: Applying the addition rule to combine mutually exclusive paths in a two-stage transfer experiment to find the distribution of a final composition.

patterns.name: Tree Diagram Construction for Sequential Dependent Events
patterns.description: Constructing and labelling a multi-stage tree diagram with branches and conditional probabilities.

patterns.name: Probability of Same-Colour Outcomes from Tree Diagram
patterns.description: Summing probabilities along mutually exclusive paths where all successive draws result in identical item categories.

patterns.name: Total Probability from Two-Stage Events
patterns.description: Problems calculating overall probability of an outcome across mutually exclusive scenarios (e.g. tree diagram branches).

patterns.name: Two-Dice Sample Space Grid and Compound Events
patterns.description: Using a two-dimensional possibility space grid for two dice to identify outcomes satisfying compound or intersection event conditions.

patterns.name: Two-Stage Binomial Model
patterns.description: Using the probability obtained from a first-stage binomial distribution as the success probability in a second-stage binomial experiment.

patterns.name: Two-Stage Die and Repeated Coin Probability
patterns.description: Finding joint probability P(Die = n and Coin = k heads) where the number of coin tosses is determined by the die outcome.

patterns.name: Two-Way Contingency Table Completion and Marginal Deduction
patterns.description: Deducing cell frequencies and marginal totals in a two-way contingency table from given partial category counts.

patterns.name: Two-Way Table Joint Probability
patterns.description: Reading and computing marginal and conditional probabilities from contingency tables.

patterns.name: Solving for Unknown Branch Probability in Tree Diagram
patterns.description: Using the law of total probability with a known marginal probability to solve a linear equation for an unknown conditional branch probability.

patterns.name: Updating Mean and Standard Deviation with Additional Observations
patterns.description: Recalculating sum of x and sum of x^2 after new observations join a dataset, then computing the pooled or updated standard deviation.

patterns.name: Identifying Upper Quartile Class Interval from Grouped Cumulative Frequencies
patterns.description: Determining which class interval contains the upper quartile by computing cumulative frequencies and identifying the interval containing the 3N/4 rank.

patterns.name: Variance of Discrete Random Variable
patterns.description: Calculating Var(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 from a distribution table.

patterns.name: Interpreting Zero Standard Deviation
patterns.description: Deducing that all observations in a dataset are identical to the mean when the standard deviation is zero.
